scenes.line2: How do you keep prod safe?
scenes.say: What's the single most important rule for scripting and automation? How do you make sure your script doesn't break production?

scenes.label: Safe
scenes.sub: Always use strict mode: exit on errors, unset vars, pipeline fails
scenes.say: In bash, always turn on strict mode. That means your script stops if anything fails, if you use a variable you forgot to set, or if a pipeline command fails.

scenes.title: Set strict mode at the top
scenes.say: Set strict mode at the very top. If you try to use an unset variable, your script will stop right there, instead of running wild.
PowerShell scripts work with real objects, so you filter and export data safely. Bash scripts just handle text, so they're fragile if the output changes.
A safe script is idempotent, can dry-run, logs its actions, fails loudly, and never hardcodes secrets. These are non-negotiable for production.

scenes.question: When should you use Python, not bash?
scenes.right: When logic, APIs, or JSON get complex, or scripts grow past fifty lines
scenes.say: Here's a trap: Should you always use bash for command-line tasks? Not really. Once your logic gets complex or you deal with APIs or JSON, switch to Python.
